method.summary: How long does one keyless documentation call to this server take, from a caller that is nobody in particular? Fifteen calls to `aws___search_documentation`: five plain-language questions inside the scope the server's own tool description claims, each sent three times, in three rounds round-robin across eight of the nine solutions measured, so a slow minute on this container's network falls across all of them rather than on one. Median 1337.5 ms, min 1161.9, max 1756.3, IQR 101.0; round medians 1374.2, 1337.5, 1308.0 ms; 0 failures. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a server-side latency. Every number includes this container, its HTTP proxy and one day's public internet from a single vantage point; three rounds notice an outlier and cannot characterise a distribution over time. Response size is not controlled and is published beside every duration (median 6912 bytes of text here): a server returning more text is doing more work on the wire, which is a property of the corpus, not of its speed. NO BASELINE, deliberately: the job says 'within the agent's turn', which is not a number, and inventing one so the coverage table resolved to supports or contradicts would be filling a cell to make the map look finished. This record is a measurement; the adjudication is the reader's. NO RANKING and no comparison with the other records filed from this run: the question sets differ because the corpora differ. The protocol was pre-registered before any call was sent.
